newsitem.title: EGYPT: HSBC says sets up bank, broker firm in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says sets up bank, broker firm in Egypt.

text.p: HSBC Investment Banking said on Thursday it had set up an investment banking branch and stock brokerage services in Cairo.

HSBC said in a statement the two firms were waiting for the approval of the local Egyptian authorities to start work. Officials at the HSBC in London could not say when they would receive the permission.
The investment banking branch will be called HSBC Investment Company (Egypt) Ltd. and the brokerage firm will be entitled HSBC James Capel Egypt Ltd.
HSBC banking group will own 60 percent of the two projects while Egyptian British Bank, an affiliate of HSBC group in Egypt, will hold the remaining 40 percent.

"The market in Egypt is very attractive and it has a lot of potential. Setting up these ventures is a sign of how big the market is," Albert Moumdijian, head of the Middle East and North Africa desk at HSBC James Capel, told Reuters.
Moumdijian said the brokerage firm was the group's first in the Middle East. HSBC already has a financial services division in Dubai.
Earlier this year, James Capel set up the first fund to trade in Egyptian equities. The Concord Fund has so far raised between $40 million and $45 million and is listed in London.
